name: Select and sell securitisation pools
summary: New leases are first funded on a bank credit line and then sold each month in pools to bank-sponsored commercial paper conduits, which is how the company refinances most of its lending. For each conduit, a securitisation analyst selects booked contracts, tests them against the conduit's eligibility criteria and concentration limits, builds the data tape, calculates the purchase price, overcollateralization and cash reserve, and gets the pool reconciled by accounting, approved by the treasurer and certified by the CFO before the conduit reviews and funds it. Data exceptions, conduit questions and file audits cause rework, and most elapsed time is waiting for month-end data, approvals, the conduit's review and the fixed settlement date.

baseline.org_archetype: A privately owned Canadian independent equipment lessor with 340 staff and about $1.5 billion of leases, funded by a syndicated bank warehouse line and monthly pool sales to three bank-sponsored ABCP conduits.
baseline.notes: Treasury has a treasurer, three securitisation and funding analysts and two treasury and cash analysts. Pool selection runs in spreadsheets fed by data warehouse queries; conduits receive tapes through their portals.

unit_of_work: one pool sale to a conduit
trigger: The month-end cut-off passes with booked contracts funded on the bank warehouse line, and the treasury cash forecast shows how much funding is needed.
end_state: The conduit has paid the purchase price, the reserve is funded, the bank line is repaid, the entries are booked and the pool is set up for monthly servicer reporting; or the purchase is deferred to the next month.

volume.seasonality: One pool per conduit each month; an extra pool when a new facility starts or a deferred pool is sold. Pools are larger after strong funding months (spring, quarter ends).

evidence.note: Organisation file process map: three conduit facilities, one sale each per month (tier C in the organisation file).

Organisation file role, cost and headcount (3); duties as in the Vault posting; cost consistent with the Job Bank NOC 11101 Ontario median of $43.27 loaded by 1.35 and scaled to 2019-2022. The rest of the analysts' time goes to servicer reports, covenant and borrowing base reporting and facility renewals.
Organisation file role; time on pool approvals is an author estimate.
Organisation file role; signing time is an author estimate.
Organisation file role; reconciliation and entries are an author estimate.

systems.name: Data warehouse and business intelligence reports
Spreadsheet models (pool cuts, borrowing base, covenants, budget, tax workpapers)
Lease management system (contracts, schedules, billing, tax codes, asset records, servicing)
General ledger and accounts payable (mid-market ERP)
Bank cash management portal for pre-authorised debit files, EFT payments and wires
Document imaging and contract file store

steps.name: Extract booked contracts not yet sold after the cut-off
steps.description: After the month-end cut-off, once bookings and month-end payments are posted, a securitisation analyst runs the data warehouse query of booked contracts still funded on the bank warehouse line, with balances, payment history, equipment, obligor, province and registration fields, and loads it into the pool workbook.

error.defect_description: Query misses late bookings or pulls contracts already sold.

evidence.note: Preparing tranches for funders monthly is in the Vault posting; minutes and the wait for month-end posting are author estimates.

steps.name: Size the sale against the cash forecast and facility headroom
steps.description: The analyst compares the treasury cash forecast and warehouse line usage with each conduit's unused commitment and the borrowing base, and decides how much this conduit should buy this month so the bank line stays within its limit.

error.defect_description: Headroom under-estimated, leaving the bank line close to its limit.

evidence.note: Author estimate; the organisation file links the cash forecast from daily cash management to this process.

steps.name: Allocate contracts to this conduit
steps.description: The analyst assigns candidate contracts to the conduit whose criteria they fit best, for example trucks to the truck facility and small-ticket office and medical equipment to a general facility, keeping the rest on the bank line or for another conduit.

error.defect_description: Contract allocated to a facility that excludes its equipment type.

evidence.note: Canadian conduits buy pools by equipment type (trucks; small- and mid-ticket equipment), and BDC's platform funds independent lessors' equipment lease securitisations (the organisation file treats it as one of the three conduits). Allocation practice and minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Test each contract against the eligibility criteria
steps.description: The analyst runs the facility's eligibility tests in the workbook: not delinquent beyond the limit, first payment made, remaining term and balloon within limits, obligor a Canadian business not in default or bankruptcy, permitted equipment type, no modification or deferral, registration perfected and minimum yield met. Ineligible contracts stay on the warehouse line.

error.defect_description: An ineligible contract (for example one modified in a payment deferral) is passed.

control.basis: Receivables purchase agreement with each conduit: contractual eligibility criteria and seller representations

evidence.note: Sponsors select only high-quality assets and rating agencies review each transaction under a Canadian equipment finance methodology. The specific tests listed are typical contractual criteria (author estimate).

steps.name: Test concentration limits and rebalance the pool
steps.description: The analyst checks the eligible pool against concentration limits on largest obligors, vendors, industries, equipment types, provinces and residual or balloon exposure, and removes or swaps contracts until every limit is met.

error.defect_description: A concentration limit calculated on the wrong base.

control.basis: Receivables purchase agreement: concentration limits that support the conduit's rating

evidence.note: Author estimate; concentration limits are standard in rated equipment securitisations.

steps.name: Resolve data exceptions with operations
steps.description: The analyst emails the funding team and data developers a list of contracts with missing registration numbers, unknown equipment codes or payment histories that do not match the schedule, and waits for corrections in the lease system.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: many changes, rerun the eligibility tests

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Build the data tape and pool schedule
steps.description: The analyst produces the contract-level data tape in the conduit's template (obligor, equipment, province, original and remaining term, payments, balance, yield, delinquency status) and the schedule of purchased contracts that will be attached to the assignment.

error.defect_description: Field mapping error, such as remaining term in the wrong unit.

evidence.note: Preparing tranches for submission to funders; template fields are an author estimate.

steps.name: Calculate the purchase price, overcollateralization and reserve
steps.description: The analyst discounts the pool's remaining payments at the conduit's discount rate to get the discounted balance, applies the advance rate to get the purchase price and works out the overcollateralization and the cash reserve deposit the company must fund, with fees and the expected excess spread.

error.defect_description: Wrong discount rate or day count in the purchase price.

evidence.note: Overcollateralization and cash reserve are seller enhancements (Bank of Canada); a peer's proceeds were about 90% of securitized balances (CWB). Minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Reconcile the pool to the lease subledger and ledger
steps.description: A lease accountant ties the pool's contract count and balances to the lease system and the general ledger, checks that no contract is already sold to another conduit or pledged elsewhere, and confirms the reserve and fee entries that will be booked.

error.defect_description: A reconciling difference is cleared without explanation.

control.basis: Internal control over financial reporting: independent reconciliation of securitised pools and a check against double sale or pledge

evidence.note: Author estimate; the organisation file lists the lease accountant in this process.

steps.name: Treasurer reviews the pool and settlement figures
steps.description: The treasurer reviews pool size, eligibility and concentration results, the purchase price and reserve, and the effect on the bank line and liquidity, and approves or asks for changes.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Treasury policy: pool and settlement prepared by an analyst and approved by the treasurer

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: CFO signs the purchase notice and officer's certificate
steps.description: The chief financial officer signs the notice of purchase and the officer's certificate repeating the seller's representations that every contract meets the eligibility criteria.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Receivables purchase agreement and board signing authorities: an authorised officer certifies the seller's representations

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Send the tape, schedule and notice to the conduit
steps.description: The analyst uploads the data tape, pool schedule, settlement calculation and signed notice to the conduit administrator's portal or secure file transfer and emails the sponsor bank's securitisation team.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Submission of tranches to funders; channel is an author estimate.

steps.name: Conduit reviews the tape
steps.description: The sponsor bank's team re-runs eligibility and concentration tests on the tape, checks the purchase price and may ask for a sample of contract files for audit.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: Sponsors select assets carefully and funder audits are part of the role (Vault). Shares and elapsed time are author estimates.

steps.name: Answer conduit questions and remove rejected contracts
steps.description: The analyst answers the sponsor's questions, takes out contracts it rejects and, if the pool changed, recalculates the purchase price for re-approval.

error.defect_description: Removed contract left on the pool schedule.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Pull contract files for the funder's file audit
steps.description: The analyst requests the sample of contract files from imaging, checks each has the signed lease, guarantee, invoice, registration and insurance evidence, and sends them to the sponsor's auditor.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Funder audits (Vault); buyers' attention to lease wording and original chattel paper (ELFA). Minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Funder's auditor reviews the sample files
steps.description: The sponsor's auditor reviews the sample files against the tape and the eligibility criteria and reports any missing documents or data mismatches.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

steps.name: Execute the assignment and flag the contracts as sold
steps.description: The analyst completes the assignment with the final schedule of purchased contracts, flags each contract in the lease system with the conduit's pool code so collections are reported and remitted to the conduit, and confirms the chattel paper is marked as assigned.

error.defect_description: A contract not flagged, so its collections are not remitted.

control.basis: PPSA: a transfer of chattel paper falls under the Act (BC PPSA s.3(a)); the conduit's interest is protected by registration and by possession of or a legend on the chattel paper

evidence.note: PPSA scope and chattel paper priority; lease securitisation structures (Legal 500). Minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Conduit funds the purchase on the settlement date
steps.description: On the facility's monthly settlement date the conduit wires the purchase price less fees. In stressed markets, as in March 2020, a sponsor can defer the purchase and the pool stays on the bank line until the next month.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: Liquidity facilities and conduit funding of committed purchases (Bank of Canada); settlement timing and deferral share are author estimates.

steps.name: Confirm the proceeds and fund the reserve account
steps.description: The analyst checks the wire in the bank portal against the settlement statement and arranges the transfer of the cash reserve deposit into the reserve account named in the facility.

error.defect_description: Reserve funded with the wrong amount.

control.basis: Receivables purchase agreement: cash reserve funded at settlement

evidence.note: Cash reserve as seller enhancement; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Send the settlement statement to treasury for the bank line paydown
steps.description: The analyst sends the settlement statement to the treasury and cash analyst, who uses the proceeds to repay the bank warehouse line in the daily cash process.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Borrowing requests and payments to funders are analyst duties (Vault); the organisation file sends funding proceeds to daily cash management.

steps.name: Record the securitisation entries
steps.description: A lease accountant books the proceeds as a securitisation liability, the reserve deposit, fees and the pool's contracts as transferred but not derecognised, and updates the securitisation subledger.

error.defect_description: Fees expensed instead of included in the liability's effective interest.

control.basis: IFRS 9 derecognition test: transfers that keep substantially all risks and rewards stay on balance sheet with a securitisation liability

evidence.note: Accounting treatment as in CWB's note 8; minutes are author estimates.

steps.name: Add the pool to servicer reporting
steps.description: The analyst adds the pool's contract list, cut-off balances and reserve to the monthly servicer report model and the warehouse pool tables, so collections, defaults and triggers are reported to the conduit from the next month.

error.defect_description: Pool cut-off balance keyed wrongly, so the first servicer report does not reconcile.

evidence.note: Monthly compliance reporting to funders (Vault); minutes are author estimates.

exceptions.name: Missing or inconsistent contract data
exceptions.description: Registration numbers, equipment codes or payment histories need correcting by operations before contracts can enter the pool.

exceptions.name: Concentration limit breached
exceptions.description: Large obligors, vendors or equipment types push the pool over a limit and contracts are reallocated.

exceptions.name: Conduit questions or rejected contracts
exceptions.description: The sponsor rejects contracts or questions the price; the pool is recalculated and re-approved.

exceptions.name: Funder file audit
exceptions.description: The sponsor samples contract files; missing documents remove contracts from the pool.

exceptions.name: Purchase deferred
exceptions.description: In stressed funding markets (for example March 2020) a sponsor defers the purchase and the contracts stay on the bank line, raising its usage.

exceptions.name: Ineligible contract found after sale
exceptions.description: A contract later found ineligible (for example a deferral granted before cut-off) must be repurchased under the seller's representations; handled in servicer reporting, not modelled here.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from month-end cut-off to settlement, entries and reporting set-up
benchmarks.population: Monthly pool sales by a Canadian independent lessor to bank-sponsored conduits, 2019-2022 (author estimate)

evidence.note: No published figure found. Monthly cadence follows from the facilities' monthly reporting and purchase cycles; about two to three weeks from cut-off to funding is an author estimate.

benchmarks.unit: cash proceeds divided by securitised lease and loan balances
benchmarks.population: CWB Financial Group equipment financing securitisations, fiscal 2021

evidence.note: Derived from the two stated figures: $962.7 million proceeds for $1,071.3 million securitised.

benchmarks.unit: share of assets backing Canadian ABCP

evidence.note: Stated in the Bank of Canada primer (source DBRS).

benchmarks.population: One Canadian truck lease conduit transaction (December 2022)

evidence.note: Stated in the rating action.

pain_points.description: Pool selection runs in spreadsheets fed by warehouse queries, so eligibility and concentration tests are rebuilt each month and errors are found by the conduit.

evidence.note: Author estimate; the organisation file lists spreadsheet pool cuts.

pain_points.description: Contract data gaps from booking (registration numbers, equipment codes) hold contracts out of pools and need chasing.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Approvals by the treasurer and CFO and the conduit's review each take days, and the fixed settlement date means a late tape waits for the next window.

evidence.note: Author estimate.

pain_points.description: Conduits depend on ABCP demand; when markets froze in March 2020 purchases could be deferred, leaving new leases on the bank line.

evidence.note: The primer describes sponsors' liquidity support and reluctance to add assets without investor demand.

sources.title: A primer on the Canadian asset-backed commercial paper market
sources.supports: Most Canadian bank-sponsored ABCP programs are multi-seller conduits buying third-party assets, including equipment leases (equipment finance 8% of assets backing Canadian ABCP in January 2024); sellers provide first-loss enhancement through overcollateralization, excess spread and a cash reserve or letter of credit sized on historical performance; for conduits using the ABCP exemption each transaction is reviewed by two rating agencies; sponsors provide liquidity facilities; monthly disclosure reporting.

sources.title: CWB Financial Group Annual Report 2021, note 8: securitization
sources.supports: A Canadian bank's equipment finance subsidiary securitized equipment financing leases and loans of $1,071.3 million in fiscal 2021 ($1,253.3 million in 2020) for cash proceeds of $962.7 million ($1,115.8 million); the transfers do not qualify for derecognition because risks are retained, so the assets stay on balance sheet and the proceeds are a securitization liability.

sources.title: DBRS confirms Lakeshore Trust at R-1 (high) (sf)
sources.supports: On 2 October 2017 a Canadian ABCP conduit added a transaction of fixed-rate and some floating-rate commercial loan and lease receivables secured by new and used small- and mid-ticket equipment; the rating agency confirms the conduit's rating when a transaction is added.

sources.title: DBRS Morningstar confirms rating on Fusion Trust's Series A Class A notes at R-1 (high) (sf)
sources.supports: On 9 December 2022 a Canadian conduit added a transaction of fixed-rate monthly, quarterly, semi-annual and annual pay lease and loan contracts secured by new and used small- and mid-ticket equipment.

sources.title: DBRS Morningstar updates Pure Grove Funding transaction 102
sources.supports: A Canadian conduit transaction backed by fixed-rate equipment lease contracts on new and used commercial trucks; program limit increased to $500 million and two more conduit lenders added (December 2022).

sources.title: Rating Canadian equipment finance securitization transactions (archived methodology)
sources.supports: A rating methodology specific to Canadian equipment finance securitizations was in force from October 2019.

sources.title: Financial/Securitization Analyst (job posting)
sources.publisher: Vault Credit Corporation on Built In Toronto
sources.supports: A Canadian equipment lessor's analyst prepares tranches for submission to funders, documents new funding tranches in the ledger, manages payments to funders, produces monthly compliance reporting, supports tranche and funder audits and makes borrowing requests.

sources.title: Asset/equipment finance and leasing (Canada)
sources.supports: Lease securitizations in Canada are more complicated than loan securitizations because selling lease rights would accelerate income; structures such as sale and sale-leaseback or concurrent leases are used.

sources.title: Personal Property Security Act [RSBC 1996] chapter 359
sources.supports: Section 3(a): the Act applies to a transfer of an account or chattel paper even when it does not secure an obligation; chattel paper means writings that evidence a monetary obligation and a security interest in or lease of specific goods.

sources.title: Ontario PPSA amended to incorporate rules relating to electronic chattel paper
sources.supports: A purchaser of chattel paper that takes possession (or control of electronic chattel paper) in the ordinary course for new value can have priority over a security interest, unless the paper indicates an assignment to someone else; rules in force 15 May 2020.

sources.title: How good is your paper?
sources.publisher: Equipment Leasing and Finance Association (EL&F magazine)
sources.supports: Capital market buyers will not buy a lease without certain clauses; many lease forms fail to designate the sole original chattel paper, which matters because the holder of original chattel paper gets priority.

sources.title: Securitization and specialty finance (indirect financing)
sources.supports: BDC's Funding Platform for Independent Lenders offers securitization, secured and structured loans to independent finance companies on mainly equipment and vehicle leases and loans; more than 20 finance companies funded (as of July 2022).

sources.title: Wages: Financial analyst in Canada (NOC 11101)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low $28.21, median $43.27, high $72.36 (2023-2024).

assumptions: Three conduit facilities each buy one pool a month (organisation file); this file describes one pool sale. Pools average about $20 million to $25 million (about 400 contracts), so most eligible new contracts leave the bank line within one to two months of booking.

Facility terms (eligibility criteria, concentration limits, advance rates, reserve levels and settlement dates) are private; the criteria listed are typical of rated equipment securitisations and are author estimates. The advance rate of about 90% is anchored on CWB's 2021 proceeds-to-balance ratio.
Conduit funding proceeds arrive inside the case (step s19) rather than starting it, so that trigger has a share of zero.
Securitised contracts stay on the balance sheet (as in CWB's note 8), so accounting records a securitisation liability; the company remains servicer and keeps the chattel paper marked as assigned.
External steps have zero touch time; the conduit's review and settlement timing are in wait_before_min.
Hands-on time per pool is about 25 to 35 hours across roles, mostly the analyst's; the analysts' other duties (servicer reports, borrowing base and covenant reporting) are separate processes.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (2019-2022 wage times 1.35).
